learning: If slalom line loss is zero and max_error is below 0.06 m, the spread was the missing piece. If slalom line loss stays at 1 per run, geometry is no longer the limiting factor, so the next test is the controller (kd) rather than the row or spread. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.14 on s-bend or slalom, the wider spread is adding jitter.
notes: Iteration 8 controller held fixed, with the Builder's ±0.08 m spread at y=0.07 m, so the race isolates the spread change. Speed stays at 0.03 m radius and the row at y=0.07 m, both supported by iterations 6, 7 and 9.
rationale: Iteration 8 (y=0.07 m, ±0.065 m, 16 mm, 0.03 m radius, 56.40) is the best raced design. Widening the spread from ±0.05 m to ±0.065 m cut s-bend line loss from 1 to 0.05 per run and raised s-bend progress from 0.155 to 0.1825. Slalom still lost the line once per run, with max_error 0.0604 m and oscillation 0.131. Iteration 9 (y=0.067 m, same spread) scored 51.11, with s-bend line loss back to 0.5 and s-bend progress down to 0.147, so the row should stay at y=0.07 m. Iteration 7 (y=0.065 m) also lost the slalom line and fell to s-bend progress 0.04, so the lead below 0.07 m is harmful. Speed stays at wheel_radius 0.03 m, because 0.04 m brought line loss back in iteration 6. The Builder's geometry for this iteration keeps the y=0.07 m row and widens the spread to the contract maximum of ±0.08 m with 16 mm footprints. I take that geometry as written. I keep the controller identical to iteration 8 (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.10, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), because the slalom oscillation of 0.13 to 0.14 has not moved across any row or spread tested. Changing kd in the same race would confound the spread test. The five weights still span the sensors and the signal stays within about ±2. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events near 0 and slalom max_error below 0.06 m. Risk: a ±0.08 m spread lowers resolution near centre, which could raise s-bend oscillation (0.127 in iteration 8) or rms_error.
